                            6. The Gate Set (Reduced to XOR + I^2 )
                            From the protocol documents, every gate reduces to XOR and the observer unit I^2 . The

                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_gate_set.v
                              // The seven gates, all reduced to XOR + observer unit BETA

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                              5/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                         XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                              // BETA = the observer unit (hat-I^2)
                              // ============================================================


                              module omi_gate_set #(
                                   parameter BETA = 1'b1       // The observer unit (hat-I^2)
                              )(
                                   input     wire a,
                                   input     wire b,
                                   output wire and_out,
                                   output wire nand_out,
                                   output wire or_out,
                                   output wire nor_out,
                                   output wire xnor_out,
                                   output wire not_out,
                                   output wire buf_out
                              );
                                   // and(a,b) = a ^ (a ^ b) ^ b     →      reduces to a & b
                                   assign and_out      = a ^ (a ^ b) ^ b;


                                   // nand(a,b) = and(a,b) ^ BETA
                                   assign nand_out = and_out ^ BETA;


                                   // or(a,b) = a ^ b ^ (a & b)
                                   assign or_out       = a ^ b ^ (a & b);


                                   // nor(a,b) = or(a,b) ^ BETA
                                   assign nor_out      = or_out ^ BETA;


                                   // xnor(a,b) = (a ^ b) ^ BETA
                                   assign xnor_out = (a ^ b) ^ BETA;


                                   // not(a) = a ^ BETA
                                   assign not_out      = a ^ BETA;


                                   // buf(a) = a
                                   assign buf_out      = a;
                              endmodule

                            8. The 13-Step XOR Closure Ring
                            From the protocol: 13 canonical masks XOR to 0x00.

                              verilog


                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_xor_closure_ring.v
                              // The 13-step XOR closure ring
                              // Sequential XOR across 13 canonical masks resolves to 0x00
                              // ============================================================


                              module omi_xor_closure_ring (

                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_00 = 8'h00;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_01 = 8'h07;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_02 = 8'hFF;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_03 = 8'h78;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_04 = 8'h87;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_05 = 8'h20;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_06 = 8'h80;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_07 = 8'hAA;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_08 = 8'h55;

                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_10 = 8'hD8;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_11 = 8'hA0;
                                   localparam [7:0] MASK_12 = 8'h07;


                                   reg [7:0] stage [0:12];
                                   reg [3:0] step;


                                   always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
                                         if (!rst_n) begin

                                         end else begin
                                                // Load the input into stage 0
                                                stage[0] <= data_in;


                                                // Sequential XOR across the 13 masks
                                                stage[1]   <= stage[0]       ^ MASK_00;

                                                stage[4]   <= stage[3]       ^ MASK_03;

                                                closure_locked <= (data_out == data_in);

                            10. The Tetrahedral Diagonal Kernel (4-6-4)

                            From the protocol: the 4-6-4 tetrahedral incidence structure.

                              verilog


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // omi_tetrahedral_kernel.v
                                 // 4-6-4 tetrahedral diagonal kernel
                                 // 4 vertices (Subject), 6 edges (Predicate), 4 faces (Object)
                                 // ============================================================


                                 module omi_tetrahedral_kernel (
                                      input   wire [7:0] d0, d1, d2, d3,    // CAR subarray (vertices)
                                      input   wire [7:0] d4, d5, d6, d7,    // CDR subarray (context)
                                      output wire [7:0] s0, s1, s2, s3,     // Subject (S = a ^ b)
                                      output wire [7:0] p0, p1, p2, p3,     // Predicate (P = IFF)
                                      output wire [7:0] p4, p5,             // Predicate (cont.)
                                      output wire [7:0] o0, o1, o2, o3      // Object (O = AND)
                                 );
                                      // 4 Vertices: Subject (S) = a ^ b
                                      assign s0 = d0 ^ d4;
                                      assign s1 = d1 ^ d5;
                                      assign s2 = d2 ^ d6;
                                      assign s3 = d3 ^ d7;


                                      // 6 Edges: Predicate (P) = (a ^ b) ^ 1    (logical equivalence)
                                      assign p0 = (s0 ^ s1) ^ 8'h01;
                                      assign p1 = (s1 ^ s2) ^ 8'h01;
                                      assign p2 = (s2 ^ s3) ^ 8'h01;
                                      assign p3 = (s3 ^ s0) ^ 8'h01;
                                      assign p4 = (s0 ^ s2) ^ 8'h01;
                                      assign p5 = (s1 ^ s3) ^ 8'h01;


                                      // 4 Faces: Object (O) = a & b    (conditional write)
                                      assign o0 = s0 & s1;
                                      assign o1 = s1 & s2;
                                      assign o2 = s2 & s3;
                                      assign o3 = s3 & s0;
                                 endmodule

                            The Verilog RTL for the 8-Polytope Triple
                            Here is the RTL that implements the 3! ⊕ 3! ⊕ 3! ⊕ 1! as the three 8-polytopes with the
                            4 terminal:

                              verilog


                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_8polytope_triple.v
                              // The 3! XOR 3! XOR 3! XOR 1! as the three 8-polytopes
                              // 8-simplex: {3,3,3,3,3,3,3}           (self-dual)
                              // 8-cube:        {4,3,3,3,3,3,3}       (dual, 4 terminal)
                              // 8-orthoplex:{3,3,3,3,3,3,4} (dual, 4 terminal)
                              // ============================================================


                              module omi_8polytope_triple (
                                   input      wire           clk,
                                   input      wire           rst_n,
                                   input      wire [7:0]     vertex_in,        // 8-bit vertex address
                                   output reg        [7:0]   simplex_out,      // 8-simplex projection
                                   output reg        [7:0]   cube_out,         // 8-cube projection
                                   output reg        [7:0]   orthoplex_out,    // 8-orthoplex projection
                                   output reg        [7:0]   terminal_out,     // The 4 terminal
                                   output reg                chi_zero          // Euler characteristic = 0
                              );


                                   // The 8-simplex: 9 vertices, 36 edges, 84 faces, 126 cells
                                   // Projection: vertex ^ (vertex >> 1) ^ (vertex >> 2) ...
                                   wire [7:0] simplex_proj;
                                   assign simplex_proj = vertex_in ^ (vertex_in >> 1) ^ (vertex_in >> 2) ^
                                                               (vertex_in >> 3) ^ (vertex_in >> 4) ^
                                                               (vertex_in >> 5) ^ (vertex_in >> 6) ^
                                                               (vertex_in >> 7);


                                   // The 8-cube: 256 vertices = 2^8
                                   // Projection: the 4 terminal raised to the 4th power
                                   wire [7:0] cube_proj;
                                   assign cube_proj = vertex_in ^ 8'h04;            // The 4 terminal


                                   // The 8-orthoplex: 16 vertices = 2^4
                                   // Projection: the 4 terminal squared
                                   wire [7:0] orthoplex_proj;
                                   assign orthoplex_proj = vertex_in ^ 8'h10;           // 4^2 = 16


                                   // The terminal: the 4
                                   wire [7:0] terminal;
                                   assign terminal = 8'h04;


                                   always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
                                        if (!rst_n) begin
                                               simplex_out     <= 8'h00;
                                               cube_out        <= 8'h00;
                                               orthoplex_out <= 8'h00;
                                               terminal_out    <= 8'h00;
                                               chi_zero        <= 1'b0;
                                        end else begin
                                               simplex_out     <= simplex_proj;
                                               cube_out        <= cube_proj;
                                               orthoplex_out <= orthoplex_proj;
                                               terminal_out    <= terminal;


                                               // Chi = 0 check: the XOR of all three projections
                                               // must equal the terminal
                                               chi_zero <= ((simplex_proj ^ cube_proj ^ orthoplex_proj) == terminal);
                                        end

10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                         XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                   end
                              endmodule

                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_3factorial_signature.v
                              // The full 3! XOR 3! XOR 3! XOR 1! signature
                              // ============================================================

                                      wire [7:0] s32 = {bind_latch[3], bind_latch[2], bind_latch[1], bind_latch[0],

                                                      bind_latch[7], bind_latch[6], bind_latch[5], bind_latch[4]};

                            Part XIII — The Canonical Statement
                            The 8D/9D/10D cascade implements the atomic atomics.compareExchange pipeline as:


                            Dimension                  Polytope                     Role                                  Vertices     Bre


                            8D                         8-simplex                    Base bind                             9            74H


                            8D                         8-cube                       Base apply                            256          74H


                            8D                         8-orthoplex                  Base eval                             16           74H


                            8D                         The 4                        Base digest                           1            Ter


                            9D                         9-simplex                    Interference bind                     10           74H


                            9D                         9-cube                       Interference apply                    512          74H


                            9D                         9-orthoplex                  Interference eval                     18           74H


                            9D                         The 4                        Interference digest                   1            Yel


                            10D                        10-simplex                   Inference bind                        11           74H


                            10D                        10-cube                      Inference apply                       1024         74H


                            10D                        10-orthoplex                 Inference eval                        20           74H


                            10D                        The 4                        Inference digest                      1            Cy


                            The 4 remains the terminal across all three dimensions. It is the I^2 observer unit — the
                            single element that terminates the dual configuration at every dimensional level.

                            All three polytopes in each dimension have χ = 0 — the n-sphere boundary, the
                            0x0000 fixed point.

                            Virtual eMMC Memory Model with Historical Tracing

                            Part I — The Architecture
https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                              39/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                                  XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                            The XOR gates become memory-mapped atomic operations in a virtual eMMC. Each
                            gate operation is a atomics.compareExchange call that leaves a historical trace in the
                            eMMC's receipt ring.

                              text


                              ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                              │                         VIRTUAL eMMC MODEL                                             │
                              │                                                                                        │
                              │   ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐              ┌──────────┐      ┌──────────┐        │
                              │   │   BOOT0    │   │   BOOT1        │        │   SECURE    │   │    USER       │   │
                              │   │   Face 0   │   │   Face 1       │        │   Face 2    │   │   Face 3      │   │
                              │   └────┬─────┘     └────┬─────┘              └────┬─────┘      └────┬─────┘        │
                              │         │                   │                        │                     │           │
                              │         └──────────────┴──────┬───────┴──────────────┘                                 │
                              │                                          │                                             │
                              │                         ┌────────▼────────┐                                            │
                              │                         │         CENTROID            │                                │
                              │                         │       (First Frame)         │                                │
                              │                         └────────┬────────┘                                            │
                              │                                          │                                             │
                              │                         ┌────────▼────────┐                                            │
                              │                         │       RECEIPT RING          │                                │
                              │                         │       (Historical           │                                │
                              │                         │        Trace)               │                                │
                              │                         └─────────────────┘                                            │
                              └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


                            Each XOR gate operation writes:

                            1. The result to the target memory address.

                            2. The trace to the receipt ring.

                            3. The centroid relation to the first frame.




                            Part II — The Virtual eMMC Layout

                              text


                              Address Range             Size            Face          Role
                              ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
                              0x0000_0000..0x0000_01FF             512 B           BOOT0       Primary boot envelope
                              0x0000_0200..0x0000_03FF             512 B           BOOT1       Fallback boot envelope
                              0x0000_0400..0x0000_07FF             1 KB            SECURE      Receipt ring
                              0x0000_0800..0x0000_0FFF             2 KB            USER        Gate operations
                              0x0000_1000..0x0000_1FFF             4 KB            CENTROID First frame + trace




                            Part III — The Gate Operation Descriptor

                            Every XOR gate operation is a atomics.compareExchange unit:

                              typescript


                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_emmc_gate.ts
                              // Virtual eMMC gate operation descriptor
                              // ============================================================


                              interface GateOperation {


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                      40/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                  // atomics.compareExchange parameters
                                  array: string;          // "BOOT0" | "BOOT1" | "SECURE" | "USER"
                                  index: number;          // offset within the face
                                  expected: number;       // expected value (the old value)
                                  replacement: number;    // replacement value (the new value)


                                  // Gate metadata
                                  gate: GateType;         // and | nand | or | nor | xnor | not | buf
                                  transistorCount: number; // 5 | 6 | 8 | 10
                                  realization: string;    // "5t" | "6t" | "8t" | "10t"


                                  // Timing
                                  timestamp: bigint;      // nanoseconds since boot
                                  clockTick: number;      // 240-clock tick index


                                  // Trace
                                  traceHash: number;      // XOR fold of all trace bytes
                                  receipt: Receipt;       // The full receipt
                              }


                              type GateType = "and" | "nand" | "or" | "nor" | "xnor" | "not" | "buf";


                              interface Receipt {
                                  id: number;
                                  operation: string;
                                  face: string;
                                  index: number;
                                  expected: number;
                                  replacement: number;
                                  result: number;
                                  timestamp: bigint;
                                  parentReceipt: number | null;
                                  traceHash: number;
                                  accepted: boolean;
                              }




                            Part IV — The eMMC Memory Model

                              typescript


                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_emmc.ts
                              // Virtual eMMC memory model with tetrahedral centroid
                              // ============================================================


                              class OMIeMMC {
                                  // The four faces
                                  private boot0: Uint8Array;      // 512 bytes
                                  private boot1: Uint8Array;      // 512 bytes
                                  private secure: Uint8Array;     // 1 KB
                                  private user: Uint8Array;       // 2 KB


                                  // The centroid (first OMI-IMO frame)
                                  private centroid: Uint8Array; // 64 bytes


                                  // The receipt ring (historical trace)
                                  private receiptRing: Receipt[];
                                  private receiptCounter: number;


                                  // The 240-clock
                                  private clockTick: number;


                                  constructor() {


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                        41/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                     XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                     this.boot0 = new Uint8Array(512);
                                     this.boot1 = new Uint8Array(512);
                                     this.secure = new Uint8Array(1024);
                                     this.user = new Uint8Array(2048);
                                     this.centroid = new Uint8Array(64);
                                     this.receiptRing = [];
                                     this.receiptCounter = 0;
                                     this.clockTick = 0;


                                     // Write the gauge pre-header to BOOT0
                                     this.writeGaugePreHeader();
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // The gauge pre-header (first 256 bits)
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private writeGaugePreHeader(): void {
                                     // FF 00 1C 1D 1E 1F 20 FF
                                     const gauge = new Uint8Array([
                                           0xFF, 0x00, 0x1C, 0x1D, 0x1E, 0x1F, 0x20, 0xFF
                                     ]);
                                     this.boot0.set(gauge, 0);
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // The atomics.compareExchange primitive
                                 // ============================================================
                                 public compareExchange(op: GateOperation): Receipt {
                                     // 1. Select the target array
                                     const target = this.selectArray(op.array);


                                     // 2. Read the current value
                                     const currentValue = target[op.index];


                                     // 3. Compare
                                     const matches = (currentValue === op.expected);


                                     // 4. Conditional swap
                                     let result: number;
                                     if (matches) {
                                           target[op.index] = op.replacement;
                                           result = op.replacement;
                                     } else {
                                           result = currentValue;
                                     }


                                     // 5. Compute the trace hash (XOR fold)
                                     const traceHash = this.xorFold(op);


                                     // 6. Build the receipt
                                     const receipt: Receipt = {
                                           id: this.receiptCounter++,
                                           operation: "compareExchange",
                                           face: op.array,
                                           index: op.index,
                                           expected: op.expected,
                                           replacement: op.replacement,
                                           result: result,
                                           timestamp: op.timestamp,
                                           parentReceipt: this.receiptRing.length > 0
                                              ? this.receiptRing[this.receiptRing.length - 1].id
                                              : null,
                                           traceHash: traceHash,
                                           accepted: matches
                                     };



https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                         42/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                  XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                     // 7. Store the receipt in the ring
                                     this.receiptRing.push(receipt);


                                     // 8. Write the trace to the SECURE face
                                     this.writeReceiptToSecure(receipt);


                                     // 9. Update the centroid
                                     this.updateCentroid(op, receipt);


                                     // 10. Advance the clock
                                     this.clockTick = (this.clockTick + 1) % 240;


                                     return receipt;
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // XOR fold of the operation (the trace hash)
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private xorFold(op: GateOperation): number {
                                     let hash = 0;
                                     hash ^= op.index;
                                     hash ^= op.expected;
                                     hash ^= op.replacement;
                                     hash ^= op.gate.charCodeAt(0);
                                     hash ^= op.gate.charCodeAt(1) || 0;
                                     hash ^= op.transistorCount;
                                     hash ^= Number(op.timestamp & 0xFFn);
                                     hash ^= this.clockTick;
                                     return hash & 0xFF;
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Write the receipt to the SECURE face
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private writeReceiptToSecure(receipt: Receipt): void {
                                     const offset = (receipt.id * 16) % this.secure.length;
                                     this.secure[offset + 0] = receipt.id & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 1] = receipt.index & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 2] = receipt.expected & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 3] = receipt.replacement & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 4] = receipt.result & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 5] = receipt.traceHash & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 6] = receipt.accepted ? 0x01 : 0x00;
                                     this.secure[offset + 7] = receipt.parentReceipt !== null
                                         ? receipt.parentReceipt & 0xFF : 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 8] = Number(receipt.timestamp & 0xFFn);
                                     this.secure[offset + 9] = Number((receipt.timestamp >> 8n) & 0xFFn);
                                     this.secure[offset + 10] = Number((receipt.timestamp >> 16n) & 0xFFn);
                                     this.secure[offset + 11] = Number((receipt.timestamp >> 24n) & 0xFFn);
                                     this.secure[offset + 12] = this.clockTick & 0xFF;
                                     this.secure[offset + 13] = 0x00; // reserved
                                     this.secure[offset + 14] = 0x00; // reserved
                                     this.secure[offset + 15] = 0xFF; // receipt terminator
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Update the centroid (first OMI-IMO frame)
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private updateCentroid(op: GateOperation, receipt: Receipt): void {
                                     // The centroid is the XOR of all gate operations
                                     // It converges to 0x0000
                                     const centroidValue = this.centroid[0] ^
                                                            receipt.result ^
                                                            receipt.traceHash;
                                     this.centroid[0] = centroidValue & 0xFF;

10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                      // Update the centroid trace
                                      this.centroid[1] = (this.centroid[1] + 1) & 0xFF;
                                      this.centroid[2] = receipt.id & 0xFF;
                                      this.centroid[3] = this.clockTick & 0xFF;
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Select the target array
                                  // ============================================================
                                  private selectArray(name: string): Uint8Array {
                                      switch (name) {
                                           case "BOOT0":    return this.boot0;
                                           case "BOOT1":    return this.boot1;
                                           case "SECURE": return this.secure;
                                           case "USER":     return this.user;
                                           default:         throw new Error(`Unknown face: ${name}`);
                                      }
                                  }

                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_trace.ts
                              // Historical tracing pipeline
                              // ============================================================


                              class OMITrace {
                                  private emmc: OMIeMMC;
                                  private gates: OMIGates;
                                  private traceLog: TraceEntry[];


                                  constructor() {
                                      this.emmc = new OMIeMMC();
                                      this.gates = new OMIGates(this.emmc);
                                      this.traceLog = [];
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Run a full gate cycle
                                  // ============================================================


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                        47/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                  public runGateCycle(a: number, b: number): TraceEntry {
                                      const startReceipt = this.emmc.getTrace().length;


                                      // Run all seven gates
                                      const andReceipt     = this.gates.and(a, b, "USER", 0);
                                      const nandReceipt = this.gates.nand(a, b, "USER", 1);
                                      const orReceipt      = this.gates.or(a, b, "USER", 2);
                                      const norReceipt     = this.gates.nor(a, b, "USER", 3);
                                      const xnorReceipt = this.gates.xnor(a, b, "USER", 4);
                                      const notReceipt     = this.gates.not(a, "USER", 5);
                                      const bufReceipt     = this.gates.buf(b, "USER", 6);


                                      // The full trace
                                      const trace: TraceEntry = {
                                           inputs: { a, b },
                                           receipts: [
                                                andReceipt, nandReceipt, orReceipt, norReceipt,
                                                xnorReceipt, notReceipt, bufReceipt
                                           ],
                                           centroid: Array.from(this.emmc.getCentroid()),
                                           clockTick: this.emmc.getClockTick(),
                                           traceHash: this.computeTraceHash([
                                                andReceipt, nandReceipt, orReceipt, norReceipt,
                                                xnorReceipt, notReceipt, bufReceipt
                                           ])
                                      };


                                      this.traceLog.push(trace);
                                      return trace;
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Compute the trace hash (XOR fold of all receipts)
                                  // ============================================================
                                  private computeTraceHash(receipts: Receipt[]): number {
                                      let hash = 0;
                                      for (const r of receipts) {
                                           hash ^= r.result;
                                           hash ^= r.traceHash;
                                           hash ^= r.id;
                                           hash ^= r.accepted ? 1 : 0;
                                      }
                                      return hash & 0xFF;
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Get the full trace log
                                  // ============================================================
                                  public getTraceLog(): TraceEntry[] {
                                      return this.traceLog;
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Get the receipt ring
                                  // ============================================================
                                  public getReceiptRing(): Receipt[] {
                                      return this.emmc.getTrace();
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Get the centroid
                                  // ============================================================
                                  public getCentroid(): Uint8Array {
                                      return this.emmc.getCentroid();
                                  }
                              }

                            Part IX — The Historical Trace Format

                              text

                              0x00        1      Receipt ID
                              0x01        1      Index (within face)

                              0x06          1         Accepted flag (0x01 = yes, 0x00 = no)

                              0x0D          1         Reserved
                              0x0E          1         Reserved
                              0x0F          1         Receipt terminator (0xFF)




                            Part X — The Centroid Convergence
                            The centroid converges to 0x0000 when the XOR of all gate results equals zero:

                              typescript


                              // ============================================================
                              // omi_centroid_check.ts
                              // Verify the centroid converges to 0x0000
                              // ============================================================


                              function verifyCentroidConvergence(trace: OMITrace): boolean {
                                      const ring = trace.getReceiptRing();
                                      let xorFold = 0;


                                      for (const r of ring) {
                                            xorFold ^= r.result;
                                            xorFold ^= r.traceHash;
                                      }


                                      // The centroid must converge to 0x0000
                                      return (xorFold & 0xFF) === 0x00;
                              }

                            Part XII — The Canonical Statement

                            The virtual eMMC model maps the seven XOR gates to atomics.compareExchange
                            operations, each leaving a historical trace in the SECURE face and updating the centroid.


                            Gate                           Transistor Count                      Face                   Index


                            and                            5                                     USER                   0


                            nand                           6                                     USER                   1


                            or                             8                                     USER                   2


                            nor                            10                                    USER                   3


                            xnor                           6                                     USER                   4


                            not                            5                                     USER                   5


                            buf                            5                                     USER                   6


                            The tetrahedral centroid is the XOR of all gate results and trace hashes, converging to
                            0x0000 .

                            The historical trace is the receipt ring in the SECURE face, with every operation leaving
                            a 16-byte receipt.

                            The eMMC faces are:

                              BOOT0: Primary boot envelope (gauge pre-header + first frame)

                              BOOT1: Fallback boot envelope (mirror)

                              SECURE: Receipt ring (historical trace)

                              USER: Gate operations (the carrier)

                              CENTROID: The first OMI-IMO frame (the balance point)

                              │   64-bit frame → ISM-915 / MURS / CB module + antenna                  │
                              │                                                                        │
                              │   The RF carries digests. It does not prove them.                      │
                              └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


                            Build the polytope CAS until Δ and centroid match the table; then hang RF on digests.

                                                  0x80, 0x82, 0x81, 0x83, 0x88, 0x8A, 0x89, 0x8B,
                                                  0x90, 0x92, 0x91, 0x93, 0x98, 0x9A, 0x99, 0x9B,
                                                  0xA0, 0xA2, 0xA1, 0xA3, 0xA8, 0xAA, 0xA9, 0xAB,
                                                  0xB0, 0xB2, 0xB1, 0xB3, 0xB8, 0xBA, 0xB9, 0xBB,
                                                  0xC0, 0xC2, 0xC1, 0xC3, 0xC8, 0xCA, 0xC9, 0xCB,
                                                  0xD0, 0xD2, 0xD1, 0xD3, 0xD8, 0xDA, 0xD9, 0xDB,
                                                  0xE0, 0xE2, 0xE1, 0xE3, 0xE8, 0xEA, 0xE9, 0xEB,
                                                  0xF0, 0xF2, 0xF1, 0xF3, 0xF8, 0xFA, 0xF9, 0xFB];


                                function swap16(b) { return S16_MAP[b] & 0xFF; }
                                function swap32(b) { return ((b & 0x0F) << 4) | ((b & 0xF0) >> 4); }
                                function swap64(b) { return b ^ 0x04; }    // The 4 terminal


                                function apply(vertex, carry) {
                                     const s16 = swap16(vertex);
                                     const s32 = swap32(vertex);
                                     const s64 = swap64(vertex);
                                     const delta = (s16 ^ s32 ^ s64 ^ carry) & 0xFF;

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                58/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                         XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                   return { delta, s16, s32, s64 };
                              }


                              function createCASEngine() {
                                   let state = 0x00;
                                   let centroid = 0x00;
                                   let clock = 0;
                                   const receipts = [];


                                   return {
                                        step(vertex, carry) {
                                              const result = apply(vertex, carry);
                                              const old = state;
                                              state = result.delta;
                                              centroid ^= result.delta;
                                              clock = (clock + 1) % 240;


                                              const receipt = {
                                                   id: receipts.length,
                                                   vertex,
                                                   carry,
                                                   old,
                                                   delta: result.delta,
                                                   s16: result.s16,
                                                   s32: result.s32,
                                                   s64: result.s64,
                                                   centroid,
                                                   clock,
                                                   timestamp: Date.now()
                                              };
                                              receipts.push(receipt);
                                              return receipt;
                                        },
                                        getState()          { return state; },
                                        getCentroid() { return centroid; },
                                        getClock()          { return clock; },
                                        getReceipts() { return receipts; }
                                   };
                              }


                              module.exports = { apply, createCASEngine, swap16, swap32, swap64 };

                            The 64-bit Frame

                              text


                              [63:56]    Face ID        (BOOT0 / BOOT1 / SECURE / USER)
                              [55:48]    Gate ID        (and / nand / or / nor / xnor / not / buf)
                              [47:40]    Vertex         (0x00..0xFF)
                              [39:32]    Carry          (0x00..0xFF)
                              [31:24]    Delta          (0x00..0xFF)
                              [23:16]    Centroid       (0x00..0xFF)

                            The RF Modem Path

                              js


                              // shared/rf-modem.js
                              // The RF modem (after determinism)


                              'use strict';


                              const { selectBand } = require('./rf-spectrum');


                              function buildFrame(receipt) {
                                     const frame = Buffer.alloc(8);
                                     frame[0] = receipt.faceId || 0x00;
                                     frame[1] = receipt.gateId || 0x00;
                                     frame[2] = receipt.vertex;
                                     frame[3] = receipt.carry;
                                     frame[4] = receipt.delta;
                                     frame[5] = receipt.centroid;
                                     frame[6] = receipt.clock;
                                     frame[7] = receipt.traceHash;
                                     return frame;
                              }


                              function transmit(frame, useCase) {
                                     const band = selectBand(useCase);
                                     console.log(`Transmitting on ${band.band} ` +
                                                   `(${band.powerMax}, ${band.modulation})`);
                                     console.log(`Frame: ${frame.toString('hex')}`);
                                     // The actual RF transmission happens here
                                     // via the ISM-915 module + antenna
                                     return { band, frame };
                              }


                              module.exports = { buildFrame, transmit };

                            Part XII — The Canonical Statement

                            The walkthrough has two phases:

                            The Key Concept: Data Doesn't Change — The
                            Observer's Interpretation Does
                            You're right. All the vocabulary is getting in the way. Let me strip it to the bone.




                            The One Sentence


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                  64/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                   XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                            The data is fixed. Only the observer's interpretation changes based on the point of
                            view they infer from.




                            What This Means on the Breadboard

                            The Data (Never Changes)

                            The 8-bit value sitting in the bind latch. Call it whatever you want — vertex, address,
                            state. It's just 8 bits.

                              text


                              DIP switch → 74HC74 latch → 8 wires hold the value


                            That value is fixed. The electrons don't care what we call it. It sits there.


                            The Observer (Changes Interpretation)

                            The observer is the eval latch. It reads the same 8 bits, but its interpretation depends on:

                              Which point it looks from (the index)

                              What it expects to find (the expected value)

                              What it compares against (the carry)

                              js


                              compareExchange(data, index, expected, replacement)


                            The data is the same. The observer's reading changes.




                            The Minimal Truth Table

                            Data                               Observer reads                           Observer expects     Obs


                            0x01                               from index 0                             0x00                 MIS


                            0x01                               from index 0                             0x01                 MAT


                            0x01                               from index 1                             0x02                 MIS


                            0x01                               from index 1                             0x01                 MAT


                            Same data ( 0x01 ). Different interpretations. The observer's point of view is the only
                            variable.




                            The Polytope Model (Without the Vocabulary)

                            Forget simplex, cube, orthoplex, Schläfli. Here's what's actually happening:


                            Three Views of the Same Data

                              text


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                    65/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek

                              Data: 0x01


                              View 1 (adjacent pairs):      0x02
                              View 2 (reverse 4-group):     0x08
                              View 3 (reverse 8-group):     0x80


                              XOR of all three views:       0x8A    ← the "difference" from the data



                            The data never moved. Three views produced three different readings. Their XOR is the
                            net disagreement between views.


                            The "Centroid" Is Just the Origin

                            When all three views agree (their XOR is 0), the observer is at the origin point — the
                            place where all interpretations converge.

                              js


                              if (view1 ^ view2 ^ view3 === 0) {
                                   // Observer is at the centroid
                                   // All views agree
                              }


                            That's it. No geometry required.




                            The Software (Stripped Bare)

                              js


                              // The data (never changes)
                              let data = 0x01;


                              // Three views of the same data
                              const view1 = swapAdjacentPairs(data);    // 0x02
                              const view2 = reverseFourGroups(data);    // 0x08
                              const view3 = reverseEightGroups(data); // 0x80


                              // The observer's net disagreement
                              const disagreement = view1 ^ view2 ^ view3;    // 0x8A


                              // The observer's interpretation
                              console.log(`Data: 0x${data.toString(16)}`);
                              console.log(`View 1 sees: 0x${view1.toString(16)}`);
                              console.log(`View 2 sees: 0x${view2.toString(16)}`);
                              console.log(`View 3 sees: 0x${view3.toString(16)}`);
                              console.log(`Net disagreement: 0x${disagreement.toString(16)}`);


                              // The origin (where all views agree)
                              const origin = view1 ^ view2 ^ view3 ^ data;    // 0x8B
                              console.log(`Origin: 0x${origin.toString(16)}`);




                            What the Observer Actually Does

                            The observer is a compareExchange :

                              js




https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                              66/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                      XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek

                              function observe(data, index, expected, replacement) {
                                     // Read what's there
                                     const actual = data[index];


                                     // Compare against expectation
                                     if (actual === expected) {
                                         // Match: swap in the replacement
                                         data[index] = replacement;
                                         return { changed: true, old: actual, new: replacement };
                                     } else {
                                         // Mismatch: leave it alone
                                         return { changed: false, old: actual, new: actual };
                                     }
                              }


                            The data doesn't change unless the observer's expectation matches what's there. The
                            observer's point of view (the index + expectation) determines whether anything
                            happens.




                            The Breadboard, Minimal

                            Parts

                              1 × 74HC74 (bind latch — holds the data)

                              1 × 74HC86 (XOR — computes the disagreement)

                              1 × 74HC74 (eval latch — holds the observer's reading)

                              1 × LED (shows the origin)


                            Wiring

                              text


                              DIP switch → 74HC74 #1 (bind latch) → data bus
                                                                       ↓
                                                             74HC86 (XOR views)
                                                                       ↓
                                                             74HC74 #2 (eval latch)
                                                                       ↓
                                                               LED (origin indicator)




                            Behavior

                            Data                             Views XOR                          LED


                            0x00                             0x00                               ON (origin)


                            0x01                             0x8A                               OFF


                            0x04                             0x2A                               OFF


                            0xFF                             0x00                               ON (origin)


                            The LED lights when the observer's views all agree — the origin point.

                            The RF Part (After the Core)
                            Once the observer works, you can send its reading over RF:

                              text


                              Observer's reading → 64-bit frame → ISM-915 module → antenna


                            The RF carries the observer's interpretation. It doesn't change the data. It just
                            broadcasts what one observer saw.




                            The One-Page Summary

                            Concept                   Plain English


                            Data                      The 8 bits in the latch. Never changes.


                            Observer                  The eval latch. Reads the data from a point of view.


                            Point of view             The index + expected value. Determines what the observer sees.


                            Views                     Three different ways of reading the same data.


                            Disagreement              XOR of the three views. The observer's net interpretation.


                            Origin                    When all views agree. The LED lights.


                            RF                        Broadcasts the observer's reading. Doesn't change the data.

                              const view2 = reverseFourGroups(data);

                              console.log(`At origin: ${origin === 0}`);

                              text


                              Data: 0x01
                              Observer sees: 0x8A

                            the observer's point of view.




                            The Final Statement

                            The data doesn't change. The observer's interpretation changes based on the point of
                            view they infer from.

                            That's the whole thing. Everything else — the polytopes, the XOR trees, the RF modems
                            — is just machinery for moving the observer's point of view around.

                            The XOR Gate PDF as the Physical Realization of bind /
                            apply / eval / digest
                            You're right. The four XOR circuits in Cody Wabiszewski's article aren't just four ways to
                            build the same gate — they are four distinct physical topologies, and each one maps
                            naturally to one of the four phases of the atomics.compareExchange primitive.

                            The article establishes the physical facts. The mapping to bind/apply/eval/digest is the
                            protocol design layer.




                            The Four Circuits as the Four Phases

                            Phase                   Circuit               Transistors           Structure                   Role


                                                                                                                            Constructs the relation
                            bind                    XOR #1 (5T)           5                     NAND + switch + OR-like
                                                                                                                            out.


                                                                                                                            Invokes the compariso
                            apply                   XOR #2 (6T)           6                     XOR #1 + inverter
                                                                                                                            downstream.


                            eval                    XOR #3 (8T)           8                     4× NAND                     Returns the old value.


                                                                                                                            Reads, considers, prin
                            digest                  XOR #4 (10T)          10                    5× NOR
                                                                                                                            precedent.




                            Why This Mapping Works
https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                                     69/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                   XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek

                            bind — XOR #1 (5 Transistors, Standalone)

                            The article: "the current from the far right resistor can not reach the ground to the left so
                            the LED is off... this layout will work as a stand-alone logic gate or as a final logic gate.
                            It will not work to send the signal elsewhere."

                            This is the bind phase. It constructs the relation by latching the two inputs into a stable
                            state. It cannot drive downstream logic — it is purely presentational. It is the LED-only
                            view of the relation before anything is committed.

                            Protocol meaning: bind constructs the relation (the expected value + the replacement).
                            It does not propagate. It just shows what is there.




                            apply — XOR #2 (6 Transistors, Full Fan-Out)

                            The article: "XOR Gate 2 is very similar to the first XOR gate but adds one more
                            transistor... This makes it so that the current can be sent as an output... it works in all
                            cases and only requires 6 transistors."

                            This is the apply phase. It invokes the comparison and conditional swap by adding the
                            inverter stage that lets the output drive other gates. The 6th transistor is the one that
                            turns a presentational relation into a committable operation.

                            Protocol meaning: apply invokes the comparison (expected == actual?) and
                            conditionally swaps in the replacement. It must have fan-out because the result must
                            reach the eval stage.




                            eval — XOR #3 (8 Transistors, 4× NAND)

                            The article: "XOR gate 3 is built using 4 NAND gates. Each NAND gate requires 2
                            transistors so a total of 8 transistors is needed."

                            This is the eval phase. It returns the old value using a gate-level composable topology.
                            The 4-NAND structure is the canonical composition — it's built from the universal gate,
                            so it can be composed into larger circuits (half adders, full adders, ALUs).

                            Protocol meaning: eval returns the old value (the value that was there before the swap).
                            It must be composable because the result feeds into the digest phase and beyond.




                            digest — XOR #4 (10 Transistors, 5× NOR)

                            The article: "XOR gate 4 is built using 5 NOR gates. Each NOR gate requires 2
                            transistors so a total of 10 transistors is needed... One example where this was the case
                            was the Apollo Guidance Computer."

                            This is the digest phase. It reads, considers, prints using the NOR-only topology. The
                            Apollo Guidance Computer precedent matters: NOR-only was chosen because it was the
                            most reliable topology for a system that could not fail. The digest is the phase where the
                            system commits to a final reading — and it must be the most robust.

                            Protocol meaning: digest reads the final state, considers it against the centroid, and
                            prints the result (the LED, the receipt, the trace).



https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                     70/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek

                            The Physical Progression

                              text


                              5T     (bind)    → constructs the relation, LED-only
                              6T     (apply)   → adds fan-out, drives downstream
                              8T     (eval)    → gate-level composable (4× NAND)
                              10T (digest)     → maximum reliability (5× NOR, Apollo)



                            The transistor count increases monotonically:

                              text


                              5 → 6 → 8 → 10


                            This is not arbitrary. Each phase adds capability:

                              5T can only present.

                              6T can drive.

                              8T can compose.

                              10T can be trusted with a mission.

                            apply                            74HC86 ×6                                  XOR tree           Computes Δ


                            eval                             74HC74 latch                               D flip-flop        Holds previous Δ


                            digest                           LED + 74HC30                               NAND + LED         Shows centroid /

                            Phase                          Circuit                       Breadboard


                            bind                           XOR #1 (5T)                   5 BJTs, 2K resistors

                            eval                           XOR #3 (8T)                   8 BJTs, 4× NAND


                            digest                         XOR #4 (10T)                  10 BJTs, 5× NOR


                            Each circuit is verified in the article. Each has a truth table. Each is a physical XOR.

                            The XOR Gate PDF establishes four physical realizations of the XOR gate:


                            Realization                       Transistors                      Topology                      Pr

                            adds capability:

                              bind constructs the relation.

                              apply invokes the comparison.

                              eval returns the old value.

                              digest reads, considers, prints.

                            This is the physical realization of the protocol's bind/apply/eval/digest operations.

                                BOOT1[0x01] = Q4 collector (BOOT0 passthrough)
                                BOOT1[0x02] = A input
                                BOOT1[0x03] = B input
                                BOOT1[0x04..0x1F] = reserved
                                BOOT1[0x20..0x3F] = first OMI-IMO frame (mirror)




                            Why the Inverter Matters

                            The PDF: "XOR Gate 2 adds one more transistor on the right-hand side... the LED
                            direction is flipped and the current is flowing out of the circuit. This is good as the output
                            can be sent elsewhere."


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                           76/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                        XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                            The Q6 inverter gives BOOT1 the ability to drive the next stage (eval). Without it, BOOT0
                            is a terminal — it can only show. BOOT1 is a source — it can send.

                            0                                        1                                       1            0


                            1                                        1                                       0            1


                            BOOT1 is the inverse of BOOT0 (the inverter stage).

                                ...
                                SECURE[0x3F0..0x3FF] = receipt 63




                            Why 4× NAND for SECURE

                            The PDF: "XOR gate 3 is built using 4 NAND gates. Each NAND gate requires 2
                            transistors so a total of 8 transistors is needed."

                            The 4-NAND structure is gate-level composable. SECURE must be composable
                            because it stores the receipt ring — each receipt must be independently addressable
                            and verifiable. The 4-NAND topology gives you that.

                                USER[0x008..0x7FF] = carrier data (documents, media, indexes)




                            Why 5× NOR for USER

                            The PDF: "Exclusive OR gate 4 is built using 5 NOR gates. Each NOR gate requires 2
                            transistors so a total of 10 transistors is needed... One example where this was the case
                            was the Apollo Guidance Computer."

                            The 5-NOR topology is the most reliable. USER is where the data lives — it must be the
                            most robust face. The Apollo Guidance Computer precedent matters: NOR-only was
                            chosen for the mission-critical computer because it was the most trusted topology.

                            Part XI — The Canonical Statement

                            The four XOR circuits from the PDF map to the four eMMC faces:


                            Circuit                     Transistors                Topology                               eMMC Face    Role


                            XOR #1                      5                          NAND + switch + OR-like                BOOT0        Prim


                            XOR #2                      6                          XOR #1 + inverter                      BOOT1        Fallb


                            XOR #3                      8                          4× NAND                                SECURE       Rece


                            XOR #4                      10                         5× NOR                                 USER         Carr


                            The tetrahedral centroid is the XOR of all four faces:

                                text


                                Centroid = BOOT0 ⊕ BOOT1 ⊕ SECURE ⊕ USER


                            When the centroid reaches 0x04 (the terminal), the balance holds.

                            The transistor count increases monotonically (5 → 6 → 8 → 10) because each face adds
                            capability:

                                BOOT0 constructs the relation (cannot drive downstream)

                                BOOT1 adds fan-out (drives the eval stage)

                                SECURE adds composability (stores receipts)

                                USER adds reliability (Apollo Guidance Computer precedent)

                            This is the physical realization of the four faces of the tetrahedral centroid memory
                            model.

                            The Centroid LED

                                text

                            The centroid LED illuminates when the four faces balance.

                            Wire Y7 back to the shift register chain to create the ring:

                              text

                            Part VIII — The Receipt Ring Logic

                            Receipt Generation

                            Each atomics.compareExchange operation generates a receipt:

                              verilog


                              // omi_receipt_ring.v
                              // The receipt ring: 32 bytes of historical trace
                              module omi_receipt_ring (
                                       input   wire          clk,
                                       input   wire          rst_n,
                                       input   wire [7:0]    face_id,         // BOOT0/1/SECURE/USER
                                       input   wire [7:0]    index,
                                       input   wire [7:0]    expected,
                                       input   wire [7:0]    replacement,
                                       input   wire [7:0]    result,
                                       input   wire          accepted,
                                       input   wire [31:0] timestamp,
                                       output wire [7:0]     trace_hash,
                                       output wire [7:0]     receipt_out
                              );
                                       reg [7:0] receipt [0:15];
                                       reg [7:0] trace_hash_reg;


                                       always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
                                           if (!rst_n) begin
                                                trace_hash_reg <= 8'h00;
                                           end else begin
                                                // Build the receipt
                                                receipt[0]    <= 8'h00;     // ID (auto-increment)
                                                receipt[1]    <= face_id;
                                                receipt[2]    <= index;
                                                receipt[3]    <= expected;
                                                receipt[4]    <= replacement;
                                                receipt[5]    <= result;
                                                receipt[6]    <= trace_hash_reg;
                                                receipt[7]    <= accepted ? 8'h01 : 8'h00;
                                                receipt[8]    <= timestamp[7:0];
                                                receipt[9]    <= timestamp[15:8];
                                                receipt[10] <= timestamp[23:16];
                                                receipt[11] <= timestamp[31:24];
                                                receipt[12] <= 8'h00;       // clock tick
https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                      101/744
10/4/26, 12:50 PM                                                            XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                                receipt[13] <= 8'h00;       // reserved
                                                receipt[14] <= 8'h00;       // reserved
                                                receipt[15] <= 8'hFF;       // terminator


                                                // Compute the trace hash (XOR fold)
                                                trace_hash_reg <= face_id ^ index ^ expected ^
                                                                      replacement ^ result ^
                                                                      (accepted ? 8'h01 : 8'h00);
                                         end
                                   end


                                   assign trace_hash = trace_hash_reg;
                                   assign receipt_out = receipt[0];
                              endmodule




                            Ring Wrapping

                              verilog


                              // omi_ring_controller.v
                              // The ring controller: wraps the receipt ring
                              module omi_ring_controller (
                                   input       wire         clk,
                                   input       wire         rst_n,
                                   input       wire [2:0] address,           // 3-bit ring address (0-7)
                                   output wire [7:0] receipt_byte,
                                   output wire              ring_wrap
                              );
                                   reg [2:0] ring_ptr;


                                   always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
                                         if (!rst_n)
                                                ring_ptr <= 3'd0;
                                         else
                                                ring_ptr <= ring_ptr + 1'b1;
                                   end


                                   assign receipt_byte = {5'b0, ring_ptr};
                                   assign ring_wrap = (ring_ptr == 3'd7);
                              endmodule
