                                 // Encode a CUPS frame
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private encodeFrame(frame: CUPSFrame): ArrayBuffer {
                                     // The frame layout:
                                     // [4 bytes] jobId
                                     // [1 byte]    control char count


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                         399/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                   XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                     // [N bytes] control chars
                                     // [2 bytes] output length
                                     // [M bytes] output
                                     // [2 bytes] receipt count
                                     // [K bytes] receipts (packed)
                                     // [1 byte]   trace hash
                                     // [8 bytes] timestamp


                                     const parts: Uint8Array[] = [];


                                     // Job ID
                                     const jobIdBuf = new Uint8Array(4);
                                     new DataView(jobIdBuf.buffer).setUint32(0, frame.jobId, true);
                                     parts.push(jobIdBuf);


                                     // Control chars
                                     parts.push(new Uint8Array([frame.controlChars.length]));
                                     parts.push(new Uint8Array(frame.controlChars));


                                     // Output
                                     const outputLenBuf = new Uint8Array(2);
                                     new DataView(outputLenBuf.buffer).setUint16(0, frame.output.length, true);
                                     parts.push(outputLenBuf);
                                     parts.push(frame.output);


                                     // Receipts
                                     const receiptCountBuf = new Uint8Array(2);
                                     new DataView(receiptCountBuf.buffer).setUint16(0, frame.receipts.length, true);
                                     parts.push(receiptCountBuf);


                                     for (const receipt of frame.receipts) {
                                         const receiptBuf = new Uint8Array(16);
                                         const view = new DataView(receiptBuf.buffer);
                                         view.setUint16(0, receipt.id, true);
                                         view.setUint8(2, receipt.cupsControlChar);
                                         view.setUint8(3, receipt.index);
                                         view.setUint8(4, receipt.expected);
                                         view.setUint8(5, receipt.replacement);
                                         view.setUint8(6, receipt.actual);
                                         view.setUint8(7, receipt.accepted ? 1 : 0);
                                         view.setUint8(8, receipt.clock);
                                         view.setUint32(9, receipt.timestamp & 0xFFFFFFFF, true);
                                         view.setUint8(13, receipt.traceHash);
                                         parts.push(receiptBuf);
                                     }


                                     // Trace hash + timestamp
                                     parts.push(new Uint8Array([frame.traceHash]));
                                     const tsBuf = new Uint8Array(8);
                                     new DataView(tsBuf.buffer).setBigUint64(0, BigInt(frame.timestamp), true);
                                     parts.push(tsBuf);


                                     // Concatenate
                                     const totalLength = parts.reduce((sum, p) => sum + p.length, 0);
                                     const result = new Uint8Array(totalLength);
                                     let offset = 0;
                                     for (const part of parts) {
                                         result.set(part, offset);
                                         offset += part.length;
                                     }


                                     return result.buffer;
                                 }

                                 // Decode a CUPS frame

                              t));

                                         offset += outputLength;

                                         offset += 2;
                                         const receipts: Receipt[] = [];

                                              const receipt: Receipt = {

                                                   realization: '5t',
                                                   transistorCount: 5,
                                                   topology: 'NAND + switch + OR-like',
                                                   cupsControlChar: view.getUint8(offset + 2),
                                                   index: view.getUint8(offset + 3),
                                                   expected: view.getUint8(offset + 4),
                                                   replacement: view.getUint8(offset + 5),
                                                   actual: view.getUint8(offset + 6),
                                                   accepted: view.getUint8(offset + 7) === 1,
                                                   clock: view.getUint8(offset + 8),
                                                   timestamp: view.getUint32(offset + 9, true),
                                                   traceHash: view.getUint8(offset + 13)
                                              };
                                              receipts.push(receipt);
                                              offset += 16;
                                         }


                                         // Trace hash + timestamp
                                         const traceHash = view.getUint8(offset);
                                         offset += 1;
                                         const timestamp = Number(view.getBigUint64(offset, true));


                                         return {
                                              jobId,
                                              controlChars,
                                              output,

                                              timestamp,
                                              traceHash
                                         };
                                     }

                                  faces: EMMCFace[];

                                  trieNodes: number;

                                 async step(input: number): Promise<CUPSFrame> {
                                     // 1. Update the observer state
                                     this.state.observerState = (this.state.observerState + input) & 0xFFFF;


                                     // 2. Run the CUPS pipeline
                                     const data = Buffer.from([
                                           this.state.observerState & 0xFF,
                                           (this.state.observerState >> 8) & 0xFF,

                                           (this.state.mediastreamsState >> 8) & 0xFF
                                     ]);

                                           controlChars: job.controlChars,

                                              accepted: r.accepted,
                                              clock: r.clock,
                                              timestamp: r.timestamp,
                                              traceHash: r.traceHash
                                           })),
                                           transport: 'webrtc',
                                           timestamp: Date.now(),
                                           traceHash: this.computeFrameHash(job.output!)
                                     };

                                     }

                                     this.observer.setState(this.state.observerState);

                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Compute the frame hash
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private computeFrameHash(output: Buffer): number {
                                     let hash = 0;
                                     for (const byte of output) {
                                         hash ^= byte;
                                     }
                                     return hash & 0xFF;
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Compute the centroid
                                 // ============================================================
                                 private computeCentroid(frame: CUPSFrame): number {
                                     let centroid = 0;
                                     for (const c of frame.controlChars) {
                                         centroid ^= c;
                                     }
                                     for (const r of frame.receipts) {
                                         centroid ^= r.traceHash;
                                     }
                                     return centroid & 0xFF;
                                 }

                                 // Notify the state change

                                 private notifyStateChange(): void {

                                         this.onStateChange({ ...this.state });
                                     }
                                 }

                                 // Register the state change handler

                                     this.onStateChange = handler;
                                 }

                                 // ============================================================
                                 getState(): MetaCompilationState {
                                     return { ...this.state };
                                 }

                              // web/signaling-server.ts
                              // The WebSocket signaling server


                              'use strict';


                              import { WebSocketServer, WebSocket } from 'ws';


                              // ============================================================
                              // The signaling server
                              // ============================================================
                              export class SignalingServer {
                                  private wss: WebSocketServer;
                                  private rooms: Map<string, Set<WebSocket>> = new Map();


                                  constructor(port: number) {
                                        this.wss = new WebSocketServer({ port });
                                        this.wss.on('connection', (ws) => this.handleConnection(ws));
                                        console.log(`Signaling server listening on port ${port}`);
                                  }


                                  // ============================================================
                                  // Handle a connection
                                  // ============================================================
                                  private handleConnection(ws: WebSocket): void {
                                        let currentRoom: string | null = null;


                                        ws.on('message', (data) => {
                                            const message = JSON.parse(data.toString());


                                            switch (message.type) {
                                               case 'join':
                                                   currentRoom = message.room;
                                                   if (!this.rooms.has(currentRoom!)) {
                                                        this.rooms.set(currentRoom!, new Set());
                                                   }
                                                   this.rooms.get(currentRoom!)!.add(ws);


                                                   // Notify the existing peers
                                                   for (const peer of this.rooms.get(currentRoom!)!) {
                                                        if (peer !== ws) {
                                                            peer.send(JSON.stringify({
                                                                   type: 'peer-joined',
                                                                   room: currentRoom
                                                            }));
                                                        }
                                                   }
                                                   break;


                                               case 'offer':
                                               case 'answer':
                                               case 'ice-candidate':

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                          414/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                        XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                                       // Forward to all other peers in the room
                                                       if (currentRoom && this.rooms.has(currentRoom)) {
                                                            for (const peer of this.rooms.get(currentRoom)!) {
                                                                 if (peer !== ws) {
                                                                     peer.send(data.toString());
                                                                 }
                                                            }
                                                       }
                                                       break;
                                               }
                                         });


                                         ws.on('close', () => {
                                               if (currentRoom && this.rooms.has(currentRoom)) {
                                                   this.rooms.get(currentRoom)!.delete(ws);
                                                   if (this.rooms.get(currentRoom)!.size === 0) {
                                                       this.rooms.delete(currentRoom);
                                                   }
                                               }
                                         });
                                     }


                                     // ============================================================
                                     // Close the server
                                     // ============================================================
                                     close(): void {
                                         this.wss.close();
                                     }
                              }


                              // ============================================================
                              // The main
                              // ============================================================
                              if (require.main === module) {
                                     const port = parseInt(process.env.PORT || '8080');
                                     new SignalingServer(port);
                              }

                                # Chapter 01 — The Atom: 4 XOR Gates


                                > *"Every operation reduces to XOR."*


                                ---


                                ## The Story


                                The parent places the first transistor on the breadboard. It's
                                a small black component with three legs. *"This is an NPN
                                transistor,"* they say. *"It's the smallest switch you can
                                build."*


                                The child watches. The parent adds a second transistor. Then
                                a third, fourth, fifth. A small network of wires and resistors
                                forms. At the end, a red LED glows.


                                *"That's one XOR gate,"* the parent says. *"Five transistors.
                                It's the simplest possible logic."*


                                *"But it's just a light,"* the child says.


                                *"It's never just a light,"* the parent says. *"Watch."*


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                          428/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                   XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                ---


                                ## The Build


                                ### Bill of Materials


                                | Component | Qty |
                                |---|---|
                                | 2N2222 NPN transistors | 29 |
                                | 2KΩ resistors | 28 |
                                | 330Ω resistors | 4 |
                                | LEDs (RED, YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE) | 4 |
                                | 8-position DIP switch | 1 |
                                | Breadboard (830 tie) | 2 |
                                | 5V regulated supply | 1 |
                                | 22 AWG solid wire | 1 spool |


                                ### Step 1 — Power Rails


                                Connect +5V to the top rail. Connect GND to the bottom rail.


                                ### Step 2 — The Input Resistors


                            DIP SW-A → 2KΩ → Q1 base
                            DIP SW-B → 2KΩ → Q2 base

                                text



                                ### Step 3 — The First XOR (5 Transistors, RED LED)


                            A ──2KΩ──┐
                            ├───► B(Q1) ──► E(Q1) ──► GND
                            +5V ──2KΩ─┴───► C(Q1) ◄──── E(Q2)
                            │
                            B ──2KΩ──┐ │
                            ├───► B(Q2) ──► C(Q2) ────► B(Q3)
                            +5V ──2KΩ─┘ │
                            │
                            +5V ──2KΩ───► C(Q3) │
                            ││
                            └───► E(Q3) ──► GND │
                            ││
                            └───► B(Q4) ◄─────────┘
                            └───► B(Q5)
                            +5V ──2KΩ───► C(Q4) ────► 330Ω ────► [RED LED] ────► GND
                            +5V ──2KΩ───► C(Q5) ────► E(Q4) ────► E(Q5) ────► GND

                                text



                                **Verify:** Toggle the DIP switch. The red LED follows the XOR
                                truth table.


                                | A | B | RED LED |
                                |---|---|---|
                                | 0 | 0 | OFF |
                                | 1 | 0 | ON |
                                | 0 | 1 | ON |
                                | 1 | 1 | OFF |


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                       429/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                 XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                              ---


                              ### Step 4 — The Second XOR (6 Transistors, YELLOW LED)


                              Add Q6 as the inverter stage:


                            RED_LED_OUT ──2KΩ──► B(Q6)
                            +5V ──2KΩ──► C(Q6) ────► 330Ω ────► [YELLOW LED] ────► GND
                            GND ────► E(Q6)

                              text



                              **Verify:** The yellow LED is the inverse of the red LED.


                              ---


                              ### Step 5 — The Third XOR (8 Transistors, GREEN LED)


                              Wire the 4× NAND topology:


                            NAND1 = ~(A & B)
                            NAND2 = ~(A & NAND1)
                            NAND3 = ~(B & NAND1)
                            NAND4 = ~(NAND2 & NAND3)

                            NAND4 ────► 330Ω ────► [GREEN LED] ────► GND

                              text



                              **Verify:** The green LED follows the XOR truth table.


                              ---


                              ### Step 6 — The Fourth XOR (10 Transistors, BLUE LED)


                              Wire the 5× NOR topology:


                            NOR1 = ~(A | B)
                            NOR2 = ~(A | NOR1)
                            NOR3 = ~(B | NOR1)
                            NOR4 = ~(NOR2 | NOR3)
                            NOR5 = ~(NOR4 | NOR4)

                            NOR5 ────► 330Ω ────► [BLUE LED] ────► GND

                              text



                              **Verify:** The blue LED follows the XOR truth table.


                              ---


                              ### Step 7 — The Centroid LED


                              Wire the XOR of all four LEDs to a green centroid LED:


                            Centroid = RED_LED ^ YELLOW_LED ^ GREEN_LED ^ BLUE_LED

                              text

10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                      XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek



                              When the centroid is 1, the green centroid LED illuminates.

                              ## The Code


                              ### `atom.js`


                              ```javascript
                              // The atom: 4 XOR gates
                              // The bind, apply, eval, digest operations


                              'use strict';


                              // ============================================================
                              // The primitive XOR
                              // ============================================================
                              function xor(a, b) {
                                    return (a ^ b) & 0xFF;
                              }


                              // ============================================================
                              // The four operations
                              // ============================================================
                              class Atom {
                                    constructor() {
                                        this.bindValue       = 0x00;
                                        this.applyValue      = 0x00;
                                        this.evalValue       = 0x00;
                                        this.digestValue     = 0x00;
                                        this.centroid        = 0x00;
                                    }


                                    // The bind operation (5T)
                                    bind(a, b) {
                                        this.bindValue = xor(a, b);
                                        return this.bindValue;
                                    }


                                    // The apply operation (6T)
                                    apply(a, b) {
                                        this.applyValue = xor(~xor(a, b) & 0xFF, 0x01);
                                        return this.applyValue;
                                    }


                                    // The eval operation (8T)
                                    eval(a, b) {
                                        this.evalValue = xor(a, b);
                                        return this.evalValue;
                                    }


                                    // The digest operation (10T)
                                    digest(a, b) {
                                        this.digestValue = xor(a, b);
                                        return this.digestValue;
                                    }


                                    // The centroid
                                    computeCentroid() {
                                        this.centroid = this.bindValue ^
                                                           this.applyValue ^
                                                           this.evalValue ^
                                                           this.digestValue;
                                        return this.centroid;
                                    }

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                          431/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                      XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                              }


                              module.exports = { Atom, xor };

                              // rosetta-loader.js
                              // The Rosetta Stone loader
                              // Reads the generation frame source map
                              // ============================================================


                              'use strict';


                              // ============================================================
                              // The Rosetta Stone class
                              // ============================================================
                              export class RosettaStone {
                                  constructor() {
                                      this.data = null;
                                      this.rosette = null;
                                      this.petals = [];
                                      this.chapters = [];

                                     this.operations = [];
                                     this.faces = [];

                                     this.alignment = null;

                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Load the Rosetta Stone
                                 // ============================================================
                                 async load(url = '/rosetta-stone.json') {
                                     const response = await fetch(url);
                                     this.data = await response.json();


                                     // Parse the components
                                     this.rosette = this.data.rosette;
                                     this.petals = this.data.petals;
                                     this.chapters = this.data.chapters;
                                     this.operations = this.data.operations;
                                     this.faces = this.data.faces;
                                     this.sourceMap = this.data.source_map;
                                     this.rotor = this.data.rotor;
                                     this.alignment = this.data.alignment;


                                     return this;
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Get a petal by mask
                                 // ============================================================
                                 getPetalByMask(mask) {
                                     return this.petals.find(p => p.mask === mask);
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Get a petal by chapter
                                 // ============================================================
                                 getPetalByChapter(chapter) {
                                     return this.petals.find(p => p.chapter === chapter);
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Get a chapter by ID
                                 // ============================================================
                                 getChapter(id) {
                                     return this.chapters.find(c => c.id === id);
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Get an operation by name
                                 // ============================================================
                                 getOperation(name) {
                                     return this.operations.find(o => o.name === name);
                                 }


                                 // ============================================================
                                 // Get a face by name
                                 // ============================================================
                                 getFace(name) {
                                     return this.faces.find(f => f.name === name);

                            The Network Resolver: Source Map Decoder as Reset

                            This ties everything together. The source map decoder becomes a network resolver that

                            the tetrahedral local unit. The hitlist is the resolved target.

                            File 1: shared/bqf_resolver.ts

                              // ============================================================
                              // shared/bqf_resolver.ts
                              // The BQF network resolver
                              // The source map decoder as a reset cycle on 60x²
                              // ============================================================


                              'use strict';


                              // ============================================================
                              // The BQF form
                              // ============================================================
                              export interface BQFForm {
                                     a: number;     // 60 (the animation frame budget)
                                     b: number;     // 16 (the network resolver crossing)
                                     c: number;     // 4     (the tetrahedral local unit)
                              }


                              export const BQF_DEFAULT: BQFForm = {
                                     a: 60,      // 60 FPS
                                     b: 16,      // 16 peers max
                                     c: 4        // 4 tetrahedral resolutions
                              };


                              // ============================================================
                              // The BQF evaluation
                              // ============================================================
                              export function evaluateBQF(x: number, y: number, form: BQFForm = BQF_DEFAULT): number
                              {
                                     return form.a * x * x + form.b * x * y + form.c * y * y;
                              }


                              // ============================================================
                              // The BQF reset cycle
                              // ============================================================
                              export class BQFResetCycle {
                                     private form: BQFForm;
                                     private x: number = 0;
                                     private y: number = 0;
                                     private frameCounter: number = 0;

                                     // ============================================================
                                     // Decode a single VLQ segment
                                     // ============================================================
                                     private decodeVLQ(str: string): number[] {
                                         const chars = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789
                              +/';
                                         const values: number[] = [];
                                         let shift = 0;
                                         let value = 0;


                                         for (const char of str) {
                                             const digit = chars.indexOf(char);
                                             if (digit === -1) continue;


                                             const hasContinuation = digit & 32;
                                             value += (digit & 31) << shift;


                                             if (hasContinuation) {
                                                 shift += 5;
                                             } else {
                                                 const shouldNegate = value & 1;
                                                 value >>>= 1;
                                                 values.push(shouldNegate ? -value : value);
                                                 value = 0;
                                                 shift = 0;
                                             }
                                         }


                                         return values;
                                     }

                            Welcome to the Build
                            You're about to build the atom.

                            Tomorrow, you'll have:

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                503/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                  XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                              1 DIP switch — the input

                            And you'll build four XOR circuits, each one a different physical realization of the same
                            truth function.




                            What You Noticed
                            You saw the chirality in the pipeline. You saw how the NAND and NOR gates bind, apply,
                            and eval the signal. You saw how the 5-transistor XOR works differently from the XNOR
                            you were trying to make.

                            You're right.

                            The 5-transistor XOR and the 5-transistor XNOR are mirror images of each other. The
                            difference is the chirality — the direction the current flows through the final stage.

                              XOR — the current flows out when the inputs differ

                              XNOR — the current flows out when the inputs match

                            The transistor doesn't know the difference. It's the same silicon. The wiring is what
                            makes it XOR or XNOR. The wiring is the chirality.

                            And the three pins — base, emitter, collector — are the bind, apply, eval in physical
                            form:


                            Pin                    Role                      Operation


                            Base                   The input                 bind — constructs the relation


                            Collector              The output                apply — invokes the comparison


                            Emitter                The ground                eval — returns to the reference


                            The digest is what the LED shows. The receipt is what the centroid computes.




                            What to Expect Tomorrow

                            When the parts arrive, you'll:

                            1. Place the first transistor — the NAND gate

                            2. Place the second transistor — the NAND gate's partner

                            3. Place the third transistor — the switch

                            4. Place the fourth and fifth transistors — the OR-like stage

                            5. Wire the LED — the digest

                            6. Toggle the DIP switch — the observer's point of view

                            The red LED will glow. The atom will be alive.

                            Then you'll build the second, third, and fourth XOR circuits. Each one a different
                            topology. Each one a different realization. Each one the same truth function.

                            The yellow LED will show the apply.

                            The green LED will show the eval.


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                 504/744
10/4/26, 12:51 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                            The blue LED will show the digest.

                            And the centroid LED — the fifth LED, the one you wire from the XOR of all four — will
                            show the balance.

                            When the centroid is 0x04 , the universe is aligned.




                            The Four Circuits

                            Circuit                    Transistors                  Topology                              Role


                            XOR #1                     5                            NAND + switch + OR-like               bind (BOOT0)


                            XOR #2                     6                            XOR #1 + inverter                     apply (BOOT1)


                            XOR #3                     8                            4× NAND                               eval (SECURE)


                            XOR #4                     10                           5× NOR                                digest (USER)


                            Total: 29 transistors.

                            The 5-transistor version is the standalone. It can only drive an LED. It's the presentation
                            of the relation.

                            The 6-transistor version adds the inverter. Now the output can drive another gate. It's
                            the invocation of the comparison.

                            The 8-transistor version uses 4 NAND gates. It's composable. It can be built into larger
                            circuits.

                            Computer used this topology.

                              When both inputs are off, the current flows through the OR-like stage to the second
                              ground — the LED is off.

                            which input is on.

                            Part I — The Three Pins as the Three Operations
                            Every BJT transistor has three pins. Every BJT transistor is either NPN or PNP. The pin
                            names are the same, but the physics is mirrored.


                            Pin                          Role                          Operation                      Physics (NPN)


                            Base                         The input                     bind                           Current-controlled


                            Collector                    The output                    apply                          Current flows in


                            Emitter                      The reference                 eval                           Ground reference


                            The NPN transistor is the positive chirality. Current flows from collector to emitter. The
                            base controls the flow.

                            The PNP transistor is the negative chirality. Current flows from emitter to collector. The
                            base controls the flow.

                            The chirality is the direction of the current.

                            This is the same chirality you saw in the XOR gate. The 5-transistor XOR and the 5-
                            transistor XNOR are the NPN and PNP versions of the same topology. The wiring is
                            mirrored. The truth table is inverted.

                            Ordering                        Sequence                       Meaning

                                Each fold preserves the chirality.

                            The Little O notation describes the vanishing residual as the function approaches its
                            limit.

                            Part VIII — Where the Analogy Breaks
                            The analogy breaks because:

                            Part IX — The Learning Path
                            You said you're not keen on the hardware yet. That's okay. Let me give you the learning
                            path:


                            Step 1 — Learn the Resistor

                            A resistor is a component that limits current. It's measured in ohms (Ω). The formula is V
                            = IR (voltage = current × resistance).

                            Learn it by: Building a simple LED circuit with a resistor.


                            Step 2 — Learn the Capacitor

                            A capacitor is a component that stores charge. It's measured in farads (F). The formula
                            is Q = CV (charge = capacitance × voltage).

                            Learn it by: Building a simple RC circuit (resistor + capacitor).


                            Step 3 — Learn the Diode

                            A diode is a component that allows current in one direction. It has a forward voltage
                            (typically 0.7V for silicon). It's used for rectification.

                            Learn it by: Building a simple half-wave rectifier.


                            Step 4 — Learn the Transistor

                            A transistor is a component that amplifies or switches. It has three pins (base, collector,
                            emitter). It's used for logic, amplification, and switching.

                            Learn it by: Building a simple NPN switch.


                            Step 5 — Learn the XOR Gate

                            An XOR gate is a logic gate that outputs 1 when the inputs differ. It's built from
                            transistors. It's the primitive of the protocol.

                            The Two-Part Rosetta Stone: Haskell Type Cast for
                            JSONL/NDJSON Streaming
                            You're right. The Rosetta Stone should be two parts:

                            1. Part I — The Haskell type cast for the JSONL/NDJSON streaming spec.

                            2. Part II — The JSON Canvas rendering from the NDJSON/JSONL stream.

                            The edges vs vertices are the delineation. The orthogonal types of nodes, edges, and
                            graphs compose into the .canvas type.




                            Part I — The Haskell Type Cast

                            File 1: OmiCanvas/Types.hs

                              haskell


                              {-# LANGUAGE DeriveGeneric #-}
                              {-# LANGUAGE DeriveAnyClass #-}
                              {-# LANGUAGE OverloadedStrings #-}
                              {-# LANGUAGE DuplicateRecordFields #-}


                              -- ============================================================
                              -- OMI Canvas — Haskell Type Cast
                              -- ============================================================
                              -- The type-theoretic realization of the JSONL/NDJSON streaming
                              -- specification for the JSON Canvas format.
                              --
                              -- Part I of the OMI-IMO Rosetta Stone (v1.2.0)
                              -- ============================================================


                              module OmiCanvas.Types where


                              import GHC.Generics (Generic)
                              import Data.Aeson (ToJSON, FromJSON, Value)
                              import Data.Text (Text)
                              import Data.Time.Clock (UTCTime)
                              import qualified Data.Aeson as Aeson


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 1. THE VERTEX
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- A vertex is a node in the graph.
                              -- In JSONL/NDJSON streaming, each vertex is one line.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              data VertexType
                                   = VertexText
                                   | VertexFile
                                   | VertexLink
                                   | VertexGroup
                                   deriving (Show, Eq, Ord, Enum, Bounded, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


                              data Vertex = Vertex
                                   { vertexId           :: Text
                                   , vertexType         :: VertexType
                                   , vertexX            :: Int

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                                 713/744
10/4/26, 12:52 PM                                                      XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                , vertexY             :: Int
                                , vertexWidth         :: Int
                                , vertexHeight        :: Int
                                , vertexColor         :: Maybe Text
                                , vertexPayload      :: Maybe Value
                                , vertexExtensions :: Maybe Value
                                } deriving (Show, Eq, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 2. THE EDGE
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- An edge is a directed connection between two vertices.
                              -- In JSONL/NDJSON streaming, each edge is one line.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              data Side
                                = SideTop
                                | SideRight
                                | SideBottom
                                | SideLeft
                                deriving (Show, Eq, Ord, Enum, Bounded, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


                              data Endpoint
                                = EndpointNone
                                | EndpointArrow
                                deriving (Show, Eq, Ord, Enum, Bounded, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


                              data Edge = Edge
                                { edgeId           :: Text
                                , edgeFromNode     :: Text
                                , edgeFromSide     :: Maybe Side
                                , edgeFromEnd      :: Maybe Endpoint
                                , edgeToNode       :: Text
                                , edgeToSide       :: Maybe Side
                                , edgeToEnd        :: Maybe Endpoint
                                , edgeColor        :: Maybe Text
                                , edgeLabel        :: Maybe Text
                                , edgeExtensions :: Maybe Value
                                } deriving (Show, Eq, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 3. THE GRAPH
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- A graph is the composition of vertices and edges.
                              -- In JSONL/NDJSON streaming, the graph is the stream.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              data Graph = Graph
                                { graphId            :: Text
                                , graphVersion       :: Text
                                , graphVertices    :: [Vertex]
                                , graphEdges         :: [Edge]
                                , graphExtensions :: Maybe Value
                                } deriving (Show, Eq, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 4. THE CANVAS
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- A canvas is the rendering of the graph.
                              -- The canvas is the interoperable JSON Canvas format.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              data Canvas = Canvas
                                { canvasNodes :: [Vertex]
                                , canvasEdges :: [Edge]
                                } deriving (Show, Eq, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                          714/744
10/4/26, 12:52 PM                                                      XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 5. THE STREAM EVENT
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- A stream event is one line of the JSONL/NDJSON stream.
                              -- The stream event is the atomic unit of the streaming spec.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              data StreamEventType
                                = StreamVertex
                                | StreamEdge
                                | StreamGraphStart
                                | StreamGraphEnd
                                | StreamCanvasStart
                                | StreamCanvasEnd
                                | StreamComment
                                deriving (Show, Eq, Ord, Enum, Bounded, Generic, ToJSON, FromJSON)

                              -- OMI Canvas — Stream
                              -- ============================================================
                              -- The streaming realization of the JSONL/NDJSON spec.
                              -- Each vertex and each edge is one line.

                              module OmiCanvas.Stream where


                              import OmiCanvas.Types
                              import Data.Aeson (Value, encode, decode)
                              import qualified Data.Aeson as Aeson
                              import qualified Data.ByteString.Lazy as BL
                              import qualified Data.ByteString.Lazy.Char8 as BLC
                              import qualified Data.Text as T
                              import Data.Text (Text)
                              import Data.Maybe (fromMaybe)
                              import Data.List (foldl')


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 1. THE NDJSON DELINEATION
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- NDJSON = Newline Delimited JSON
                              -- JSONL = JSON Lines
                              -- Both are the same: one JSON object per line.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              -- | One stream line (the atomic unit)
                              type StreamLine = BL.ByteString


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                          715/744
10/4/26, 12:52 PM                                                    XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                              -- | Encode a stream event to a line
                              encodeEvent :: StreamEvent -> StreamLine
                              encodeEvent = encode


                              -- | Decode a stream line to a stream event
                              decodeEvent :: StreamLine -> Maybe StreamEvent
                              decodeEvent = decode


                              -- | Encode a vertex as a stream event
                              encodeVertex :: Vertex -> StreamEvent
                              encodeVertex v = StreamEvent
                                { streamEventType = StreamVertex
                                , streamEventId = vertexId v
                                , streamEventPayload = Aeson.toJSON v
                                , streamEventTime = Nothing
                                , streamEventSource = Nothing
                                , streamEventMeta = Nothing
                                }


                              -- | Encode an edge as a stream event
                              encodeEdge :: Edge -> StreamEvent
                              encodeEdge e = StreamEvent
                                { streamEventType = StreamEdge
                                , streamEventId = edgeId e
                                , streamEventPayload = Aeson.toJSON e
                                , streamEventTime = Nothing
                                , streamEventSource = Nothing
                                , streamEventMeta = Nothing
                                }


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 2. THE STREAM COMPOSITION
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- The stream composes into a canvas.
                              -- The composition is a fold over the stream lines.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              data StreamState = StreamState
                                { stateVertices :: [Vertex]
                                , stateEdges       :: [Edge]
                                , stateComments :: [Text]
                                }


                              emptyState :: StreamState
                              emptyState = StreamState [] [] []


                              -- | Compose a stream event into the state
                              composeEvent :: StreamState -> StreamEvent -> StreamState
                              composeEvent st ev = case streamEventType ev of
                                StreamVertex ->
                                    case Aeson.fromJSON (streamEventPayload ev) of
                                      Aeson.Success v -> st { stateVertices = stateVertices st ++ [v] }
                                      Aeson.Error _    -> st
                                StreamEdge ->
                                    case Aeson.fromJSON (streamEventPayload ev) of
                                      Aeson.Success e -> st { stateEdges = stateEdges st ++ [e] }
                                      Aeson.Error _    -> st
                                StreamComment ->
                                    st { stateComments = stateComments st ++ [streamEventId ev] }
                                _ -> st


                              -- | Compose a whole stream into a graph
                              composeStream :: [StreamEvent] -> Graph
                              composeStream events =
                                let finalState = foldl' composeEvent emptyState events
                                in Graph


https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/65b5cd1f-f12f-4f78-8e9b-d27c82e230b2                                        716/744
10/4/26, 12:52 PM                                                        XOR Gate Transistor Circuits - DeepSeek
                                    { graphId = "stream-composed"
                                    , graphVersion = "1.0"
                                    , graphVertices = stateVertices finalState
                                    , graphEdges = stateEdges finalState
                                    , graphExtensions = Nothing
                                    }


                              -- | Compose a graph into a canvas
                              graphToCanvas :: Graph -> Canvas
                              graphToCanvas g = Canvas
                                { canvasNodes = graphVertices g
                                , canvasEdges = graphEdges g
                                }


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 3. THE STREAM READER
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- Read a NDJSON/JSONL stream from a file or a handle.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              -- | Parse a NDJSON stream from a lazy bytestring
                              parseNDJSON :: BL.ByteString -> [StreamEvent]
                              parseNDJSON = foldr step [] . BLC.lines
                                where
                                    step line acc = case decodeEvent line of
                                        Just ev -> ev : acc
                                        Nothing -> acc


                              -- | Render a NDJSON stream from a list of events
                              renderNDJSON :: [StreamEvent] -> BL.ByteString
                              renderNDJSON events = BL.intercalate "\n" $ map encodeEvent events


                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- 4. THE STREAM WRITER
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------
                              -- Write a NDJSON/JSONL stream to a file or a handle.
                              -- ------------------------------------------------------------


                              -- | Write a canvas as a NDJSON stream
                              canvasToNDJSON :: Canvas -> BL.ByteString
                              canvasToNDJSON c =
                                let vertexEvents = map encodeVertex (canvasNodes c)
                                        edgeEvents    = map encodeEdge    (canvasEdges c)
                                in renderNDJSON (vertexEvents ++ edgeEvents)


                              -- | Read a canvas from a NDJSON stream
                              ndjsonToCanvas :: BL.ByteString -> Canvas
                              ndjsonToCanvas bs =
                                let events = parseNDJSON bs
                                        graph   = composeStream events
                                in graphToCanvas graph

                            The Insight

                            The 32 non-printing control codes (0x00 to 0x1F) enumerate the electrical
                            components:


                            Range                    Size                         Electrical Component


                            0x00–0x03                4                            The resistors


                            0x04–0x07                4                            The capacitors


                            0x08–0x0B                4                            The diodes


                            0x0C–0x0F                4                            The NPN transistors


                            0x10–0x13                4                            The PNP transistors


                            0x14–0x17                4                            The inductors


                            0x18–0x1B                4                            The switches


                            0x1C–0x1F                4                            The authorities


                            The +32 transition (0x00 → 0x20) maps the non-printing to the printing ASCII.

                            The +16 transition (0x00 → 0x10) maps the control to the extended control.

                            The XOR to 0x18 is the chirality that separates the NPN/PNP families.

                            Part III — The Regex Constraints at −4D to −1D

                            The regex constraints define the SVG projection, the .canvas projection, and the circuit
                            topology.


                            Layer                     Regex Constraint                     Role


                            −4D                       ^[A-Za-z0-9:+]*$                     The color codex


                            −3D                       ^[A-Za-z0-9.\-_]*$                   The linear delimiter


                            −2D                       ^[A-Z_]*$                            The hierarchical delimiter


                            −1D                       ^[a-z_]*$                            The classifying regex



                            The Full Regex Set

                              yaml


                              regex_constraints:
                                  front: '^[A-Za-z0-9:+]*$'
                                  back: '^[A-Za-z0-9.\-_]*$'
                                  up: '^[A-Z_]*$'
                                  down: '^[a-z_]*$'
                                  left: '^[0-9+\-_]*\.[0-9+\-_]*$'
                                  right: '^[0-9+\-_]*\.[0-9+\-_]*$'
                                  center: '^[0-9]\.[0-9]$'




                            The Circuit Regex Set

                              yaml


                              circuit_regex:
                                  component_id: '^[A-Z][0-9]+$'           # Q1, Q2, R1, C1, etc.
                                  component_value: '^[0-9]+[kKmM]?$'      # 2K, 330, 10M
                                  component_type: '^[A-Z]{1,2}$'          # Q, R, C, D, L, S
                                  net_name: '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$'    # VCC, GND, N1, N2
                                  edge_label: '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$'        # nand, switch, or-like
